text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Hage Geingob said in the National Assembly that the so-called General Motors assembly plant deal had not yet been finished.
- Complaints about Cash Paymaster Services, which won the tender for privatisation of the government's social pension scheme, are being dealt with regularly, says a health department official.
- International Construction has withdrawn court action against Stocks and Stocks, the public works, transport and commumications ministry and the Tender Board.
- Prime Minister Hage Geingob confirmed in parliament that the government "intends" to purchase 800 general motors vehicles worth N$ 138 million.
